title: U.S. House · Colorado's 2nd District
area: North-central Colorado, including Boulder, Fort Collins and the western mountain corridor.

context.text: Incumbent Joe Neguse advanced unopposed from the Democratic primary. Kelley Dennison defeated Christina Blunt in the Republican primary. This seat is a Democratic stronghold.

candidates.name: Joe Neguse
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary, unopposed

summary.text: Joe Neguse is the Democratic incumbent for Colorado's 2nd District, first elected in 2018. A University of Colorado graduate, he co-founded the civic group New Era Colorado, served on the University of Colorado Board of Regents, and led Colorado's consumer-protection agency before entering Congress. In the House he serves on the Natural Resources, Judiciary and Rules committees and, since March 2024, as Assistant Democratic Leader.

background.text: Born May 13, 1984, in Bakersfield, California; his parents immigrated from Eritrea, and the family moved to Colorado when he was six.
Earned a B.S. in political science and economics (summa cum laude) from the University of Colorado Boulder and a J.D. from the University of Colorado School of Law.
Co-founded New Era Colorado, a youth civic-engagement organization.
Elected in 2008 to the University of Colorado Board of Regents for the 2nd Congressional District, serving a six-year term.
Served in Gov. John Hickenlooper's cabinet as executive director of the Colorado Department of Regulatory Agencies (2015-2017).
Elected to the U.S. House in 2018 and is Colorado's first Black member of Congress, according to his official biography.
Serves on the Natural Resources, Judiciary and Rules committees and is ranking member of the Federal Lands subcommittee, per his official biography.
Elected House Assistant Minority Leader (Assistant Democratic Leader) in March 2024.
According to his office, he was named among the most effective lawmakers by the Center for Effective Lawmaking and has authored laws on public lands, rural schools and small business.
Lives in Lafayette, Colorado, with his wife, Andrea, and their two children, according to his official biography.

priorities.text: Gun violence prevention, as Vice Chair of the House Gun Violence Prevention Task Force, including calling for reinstating a federal assault weapons ban.
Climate action and public-lands conservation, as a member of the (former) House Select Committee on the Climate Crisis and the House Natural Resources Committee.
Expanding public health coverage, as a sponsor of the Medicare for All Act and Vice Chair of the Medicare for All Caucus, including a proposal to lower the Medicare eligibility age to 60.

positions.summary: Has called for reinstating a federal assault weapons ban and is a cosponsor of the Bipartisan Background Checks Act, the Enhanced Background Checks Act (closing the "Charleston loophole"), an assault weapons ban bill, and a red-flag-law bill allowing courts to temporarily bar at-risk individuals from possessing firearms.
Is a sponsor of the Medicare for All Act and Vice Chair of the Medicare for All Caucus, and has proposed lowering the Medicare eligibility age to 60.

Has served on the House Select Committee on the Climate Crisis and introduced multiple bills addressing climate change and clean energy, including the SOLAR Edge Act to incentivize residential solar installation and the 21st Century Conservation Corps Act.

Returned to federal court with colleagues after the Trump-Vance administration re-imposed a policy blocking unannounced congressional oversight of immigration detention facilities, and has previously called for ending contracts with private immigration detention centers and supported sanctuary families facing removal.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Natural Resources (Federal Lands Subcommittee), Committee on Judiciary, and Committee on Rules in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

summary.text: Kelley Dennison is the Republican nominee for Colorado's 2nd District, a 27-year-old licensed massage therapist and small-business owner who grew up in Estes Park. A first-time candidate, she won the June 30, 2026 Republican primary. Her campaign materials emphasize economic affordability, energy, small businesses and conservation of Colorado's headwaters.

background.text: A Colorado native from Estes Park; reported as 27 years old and adopted by parents nearly five decades older, raised in a household she describes as "Kennedy Democrats."
Earned a high school diploma from Estes Park High School.
Graduated from the Academy of Natural Therapy in 2023.
Works as a licensed massage therapist who operates a private practice and works as a contractor in Windsor, Colorado.
Describes herself as a business owner and activist; the Estes Valley Voice reports she worked as a campaign staffer for another Republican candidate (Adam DeRito) before running.
Entered the Republican primary days before the filing deadline as a first-time candidate and won the June 30, 2026 nomination.

priorities.text: Economic affordability: cites rising housing costs, gas, inflation and property taxes, and proposes strengthening small businesses and easing barriers to home ownership.
Environmental stewardship of Colorado's headwaters, rivers and forests, favoring 'responsible' land use and locally rooted stewardship over what she calls top-down mandates.
Pro-family policy, including protecting parental rights in education and health care decisions and support for veterans and seniors.

positions.summary: Calls for making it easier for families to afford homes while also favoring 'responsible' economic growth and locally-rooted land-use policy rather than top-down mandates.
Lists 'parental rights in education' as a passion area, favoring parents as informed and empowered partners in children's education decisions.

candidates.name: Gaylon Kent

summary.text: Gaylon Kent is the Libertarian Party candidate for Colorado's 2nd District. He is a writer who lives in Hayden, works as a hotel night auditor and hospital security officer, and served in the U.S. Navy in the 1980s. He has run for federal office as a Libertarian several times and describes himself as the "peace candidate."

background.text: Born in Los Angeles, California; earned a high school diploma from Los Angeles Lutheran High School.
Served in the U.S. Navy from 1983 to 1987.
Works as a writer and author; in his 2026 survey he says he works as a hotel night auditor and in hospital security, and lives in Hayden, Colorado.
In his 2024 survey he says he was the Libertarian nominee for U.S. Senate in 2014 and for U.S. House in District 3 in 2016 and 2018, and the Libertarian nominee in this district in 2024.
Ballotpedia lists him as affiliated with the American Legion as of 2024.
